game.name: Super Mario 64
game.rules:
**IMPORTANT:** To see specific rules for N64/VC/EMU subcategories, check the 'Category Rules' tab as well.

## Video Requirements:

All submissions requires a full video of the run, including game audio. 

## 

- The whole run should be in one segment
- Game audio must be audible (runs may be accepted with the 'Verified: No' flag for: extremely low game audio, constant music playback, and other related avoidable situations)
- The video link MUST embed on the run page (e.g. no URL shorteners or sketchy file sharing sites)
- VODs should persist indefinitely (e.g. Highlight instead of Past Broadcast)
- Dynamic HUD elements should not be obscured or omitted (e.g. coin count, star count, life count)

## Auto-rejection (SM64 Moderation Bot):

We use a bot to auto-reject runs which do not fill out the submission forms correctly, since we can't perform data validation via the submission form. If your run is auto-rejected, simply edit the submission with the fixes and resubmit the run. This has no bearing on the validity of your run (which may or may not be rejected for other reasons).

To avoid auto-rejection:

- Do not include milliseconds in your final time.
- Make sure the Platform matches the Platform subcategory (N64/VC/EMU)
- Make sure you highlight your twitch VOD.
- Leave the "Verified" flag set to "Yes"

## Good Faith Submissions

Runs are expected to be performed in good faith and may be rejected based on mod discretion if performed otherwise.  Examples include, but are not limited to: extended stalling to achieve a specific time; intentionally attempting to get the last place time on the leaderboard and/or the longest time possible; or attempting to exploit technicalities in the written category rules in a manner contrary to the spirit of the category. This means that long runs and/or runs with breaks will be considered in good faith so long as effort is still being made.

newsList.title: Replacing Expiring Twitch VODs
newsList.body:
If you wish to replace your twitch highlights with reuploads, please edit your already verified run rather than deleting the verified run and making a new submission. This makes it a lot easier for us to track which submissions are reuploads and should be less work on your part as well.

relatedGames.rules:
## General Rules

Video is required for all new submissions, the video quality must be sufficient to verify that the objectives of the category are satisfied.

Unless explicitly stated, all category extensions follow the same "rules" as 16 star, meaning SBLJ or any form of skipping the 30 star door other than MIPS clipping is banned.

## Emulator

Emulator submissions follow the same restrictions as the main leaderboards. Check the rules on the main leaderboards, if you need help setting up Project64, check the emulator setup guide: https://wermi.neocities.org/emuguide/

## Codes

For categories which allow codes, ONLY the listed codes are allowed to be active. Any extra codes, even cosmetic ones, are not allowed. Abusing unintended effects caused by the codes to gain advantages in a run is generally banned.

categories.name: Stage RTA
categories.rules:
# General Rules (updated 10/16/2023)

Stage RTA generally follows the same rules as those listed under the main Game Rules with the addition of the following:

- You must start your run from the star select menu on the relevant stage.
- Usamune/Everdrive/Gameshark are allowed, but certain codes are banned (see below for specifics). If you use one of these methods for gameplay, please set the Codes field to 'Yes' when submitting.

# Timing

Timing starts on star select and ends after grabbing the 7th star of the stage. For exact retiming, the first fade frame is 0.06 on the timer. If using Usamune, the first frame the Stage RTA timer says START is 0.03. Timing ends on the first frame of stardust upon grabbing the final star.

#  Video

All submitted Stage RTA videos must be reasonably trimmed down to the actual attempt to make it easier to find for both the verifier and the viewer. For example, full 120 star runs with just a timestamp will not be accepted on this leaderboard.

# Allowed Codes

If using the latest Usamune (latest version: v1.93 as of this writing), it is strongly recommended to use the Stage RTA preset (MENU > MISC > PRESET > STGRTA). If you choose to use your own settings or only have a Gameshark, the following codes are allowed:

- Star Select (RESET > LBUTTON/LxR > SSLECT)
- Manual Timer + Star-Grab/X-Cam Timer (TIMER > STOP/DISPLAY > GRAB/XCAM)
- Real Time Timer (TIMER > REALTMR)
- Make Timer Display Centiseconds (only relevant to Gameshark)
- Lag Frame Counter (HUD > LIFE > LAG or HUD > STAR > LAG)
- Display Lag Frame Counter as Life Count (only relevant to Gameshark)
- Automatically Reset Timer at Star Select (only relevant to Gameshark)
- Automatically Reset Counter at Star Select (only relevant to Gameshark)
- Modifying the Timer Coordinates (TIMER > TMRPOSI > LEFT)
- Setting the starting mission (RESET > DEFMISS)
- Stars always yellow (MISC > *COLOR > YELLOW)

# Banned Codes/Settings

The following settings/codes are banned and using them will result in your run being rejected. In Usamune, these should be set to "OFF" or changed to an appropriate value:

- Always Display Timer (TIMER > DISPLAY > ALWAYS)
- Fade Timer (TIMER > FADETMR)
- Section Timer (TIMER > SECTMR)
- Misc Timer (MISCT > MISCTMR)
- Level Reset/Entry (RESET > LBUTTON/LxR > LRESET/LENTRY )
- Attempt Counter (RESET > ATTEMPT)
- Savestates (RESET > SSTATES)
- All HUD modifications except for LAG display (HUD > *)
- Memory viewer (HUD > MEMORY)
- Automatic Menu (MISC > IGMENU)
- No Music (MISC > MUSIC)
- Nonstop (MISC > NSTOP)
- All of these settings under the 'STAGE' tab in Usamune must be set to 'NORMAL': CCMPENG, DDDSUB, DDDMANT, JRBMIST, STGTXT, STARTXT
- Any codes that change vanilla visuals/colors (e.g. Mario color swaps), and any other modifications to the Usamune ROM

Generally, any codes which display the timer before grabbing the star, or display information which can be used to your advantage (speed display, wall-kick frames, dust frames, input values, etc.) are banned. Using codes which are not listed as explicitly allowed or banned here may result in your run being rejected. It is strongly recommended to use the Usamune preset.

values.name: N64
values.rules:
# N64 Rules

Runs verified to the N64 subcategory are done on Nintendo 64 consoles with official carts.

## Authenticity (full game only)

- Everdrive/flash carts are banned
- NTSC to PAL conversion is banned
- Using modified ROMs or reproduction carts is banned

## Retiming (full game only)

For exact retiming of N64 runs, the first frame of the Super Mario 64 logo should appear at 1.33 seconds.

## Controller Restrictions

For console runs re-mapping of controller inputs/outputs is allowed, with the following restrictions:

The re-mapping scheme at the beginning of the run must remain for the entirety of the run. That is, a runner using a controller that maps buttons to analog inputs (e.g. Boxx) must use a controller with that re-mapping scheme for the duration of the run. Swapping controllers to ones with the same re-mapping scheme (e.g. swapping from OEM N64 to Hori Mini Pad) is acceptable.

There should be no overlap in mapping analog to analog inputs or analog to digital inputs. (You cannot map analog up to both a control stick and the “A” button.) Digital inputs can be mapped to multiple buttons as it does not provide a competitive advantage. (The hori has two Z buttons, but only one press is registered if both buttons are pressed simultaneously. This is acceptable.)

values.name: VC
values.rules:
# VC Rules

Runs verified on the VC subcategory include the Wii VC, Wii U VC and Switch NSO releases of SM64.

## Authenticity (full game only)

- Official Wii VC versions are allowed.
- Official Wii U VC versions are allowed.
- Official Switch NSO releases are allowed.
- Injecting unofficial versions such as JP 1.0 is banned.
- Modified ROMs/WADs are banned

Runs done on the 3d All Star version should be submitted to the leaderboards found on [Category Extensions](https://www.speedrun.com/sm64ce).

## Retiming (full game only)

For exact retiming of Wii U VC and Switch NSO runs, the first frame of the Super Mario 64 logo should appear at 1.33 seconds.

For Wii VC timing starts on reset (the first frame the screen goes black before the classic controller text/mario logo) and ends when the big star is collected at the end of the game.

## Controller Restrictions

For console runs re-mapping of controller inputs/outputs is allowed, with the following restrictions:

The re-mapping scheme at the beginning of the run must remain for the entirety of the run. That is, a runner using a controller that maps buttons to analog inputs (e.g. Boxx) must use a controller with that re-mapping scheme for the duration of the run. Swapping controllers to ones with the same re-mapping scheme (e.g. swapping from OEM N64 to Hori Mini Pad) is acceptable.

There should be no overlap in mapping analog to analog inputs or analog to digital inputs. (You cannot map analog up to both a control stick and the “A” button.) Digital inputs can be mapped to multiple buttons as it does not provide a competitive advantage. (The hori has two Z buttons, but only one press is registered if both buttons are pressed simultaneously. This is acceptable.)

values.name: EMU
values.rules:
# EMU Rules

Runs verified to the EMU subcategory are done on unmodified ROMs using one of the allowed emulators.

## Allowed Emulators

The **only** allowed emulators are as follows:

- Project64 v1.6.x [(Windows)]([https://wermi.neocities.org/emuguide/getting_emu/](https://wermi.neocities.org/emuguide/getting_emu/))
- Rosalie's Mupen GUI v0.5.x+ [(Windows/Linux)]([https://github.com/Rosalie241/RMG/releases](https://github.com/Rosalie241/RMG/releases))
- OpenEmu v2.x+ [(Mac)]([https://openemu.org/](https://openemu.org/))

Any emulator & version not listed above is banned. Any ROM modifications or emulator settings that cause non-vanilla behavior are banned (e.g. widescreen). If using Rosalie's Mupen GUI or OpenEmu it is recommend to make a note in the run description when submitting your runs.

## Required Settings

Generally, you do not want to tweak emulator settings without good reason. Project 64 1.6 users should follow the emulator setup guide. For every emulator run, we inspect the reset, load times, save lag and emulated lag to ensure that it is consistent with properly configured build of one of the allowed emulators. If your settings don't seem to be consistent, or your video quality is too poor for us to check these things, your run may be rejected or we may reach out to try to determine the inconsistencies.

The following are settings which are commonly misconfigured:

- The **Counter Factor** setting should be set to 1 (Edit Game Settings > Rom Settings), by default this is set to 2. This removes all emulated lag from the game. This is a new rule as of March 22nd, 2022 (Project 64) and February 16th, 2024 (Rosalie's Mupen GUI), OpenEMU users see the note below this list.
- The **Limit FPS** setting must be toggled (System > Limit FPS), this is on by default but you can accidentally toggle it off with F4 (which is next to F5, the load state hotkey).
- The **Default Save type** setting should be left as "Use First Used Save Type" (Edit Game Settings > Rom Settings), this is the default setting. There is no reason to change this but it has become an increasingly common rejection reason.

## 

Note: If you are using OpenEmu, there is currently no way to remove emulated lag. You should mention usage of OpenEmu in your submission text to save us some time when verifying and avoid rejection.

## Retiming (full game only)

Timing starts from power on (loading the ROM) or reset (pressing F1) and ends when the big star is collected at the end of the game (the first frame that the star bursts into dust). You cannot use a savestate to restart a run, since any possible savestate would cut off the start of the run. To quickly clear your files in a way that won't invalidate your runs, savestate to a clean file and then press reset.

For exact retiming of EMU runs, the first frame of the Super Mario 64 logo should appear at 1.33 seconds.
